brief: Goldman's Pasquariello lays out his year-end directional framework. Near-term (through 2026) he sees risk/reward skewed positive: positioning has been cleansed, seasonals are favorable (since 1952, the last seven weeks of the year rally 69% of the time, averaging 2.1%), AI demand evidence from TSMC and CoreWeave stayed strong despite a rough week for AI infrastructure stocks, and nominal GDP growth is running above trend and accelerating. He flags a disjunction between how the market feels and how indices perform: the market's AI bellwether stock lost over $500bn in market cap and 2-year yields backed up 33bps on inflation concerns, yet NDX still rallied 3.5% the same week. Looking to 2027, he expects it to get more complicated: the AI buildout's uninterrupted pace is now at political/regulatory risk, core CPI is broadening not just sticky, and 2027 should bring the largest net Treasury supply increase since 2000. His conclusion: positive skew through year-end, primary uptrend intact, but more volatility and less upward convexity into 2027, i.e., a seesaw market grinding out smaller gains. Separately, positioning has been liquidated hard since October, including the franchise's biggest AI-stock sale in four years, leaving PB net exposure in the 3rd percentile.
